text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Mubarak and Arafat discuss ways to save the peace process and to stop Israeli settlements. Foreign Minister Moussa says after meeting that Mubarak's suggestion to temporarily freeze settlements is aimed at completely halting settlements so that negotiations can restart. Arafat says Israel violated peace deal signed in Washington.
- Cabinet forms two working teams to implement cooperation agreement with Morocco. New oil discovery in Gulf of Suez.
- Moussa tells al-Ahram that Israel's policy will lead to breakdown of peace process. He says that Turkey's Middle East policies raise many questions.
- Mubarak to head meeting of supreme council of exports.
- Meeting between Grand Sheikh of al-Azhar and British crown prince encourages tolerance between religions.
- Mubarak calls Jordan's King Hussein and Israeli President Ezer Weizman on peace process.
- International Finance Corporation invests $200 million in Egypt per year. Deputy head of IFC says Egypt is on verge of big development boom.
- Huge reception for Youssef Chahine at Cairo airport. Director was awarded Canned film festival 50th anniversary award for his life's work.
